correctness.rationale: With the frozen angular-frequency convention, integrating the 3-ball slices gives the positive prefactor 8πα⁻³s⁻³ multiplying F. The convolution of cos(ux) with sin(sx), evaluated at 1, is s(cos u−cos s)/(s²−u²); applying 1−s∂s gives F=s²N/(s²−u²)². Taylor expansion in u at u=±s gives the removable value (sin s−s cos s)/4; the axial slice s=0 reduces to the positive cubic-weight cosine integral by |sin(u/2)|<|u/2|. For 0<s<π, N/(2s) is the strict tangent deficit of cos√t at t=s², using strict convexity up to π² and that the tangent is below −1 thereafter. At s=π, N=2π(1+cos u), with ±π removed from the alleged zeros by the positive resonance value. For a closest zero the comparison with (3π,π) gives |u|≤3π and π≤s≤π√(1+9/α²). The lower bound is strict because u=0,s=π is not a zero. At (3π,π), N_s=−8π², N_u=0, N_uu=2π, so the true local curve has s=π+(u−3π)²/(8π)+O((u−3π)³); moving slightly left strictly improves the upper bound at each finite α. Compact localization forces any positive-u minimizer onto that curve as α grows. The second derivative of s(u)² at the limit is 1/2; analytic stationarity for s(u)²+α⁻²u² then gives the stated shifts and the −36π²/α² term in κ². Finally, volume 2π/(3α³) gives the claimed J₂-root threshold by comparing to the ball; the strict lower bound even suffices at equality of the stated threshold.
residual_risks: Uniqueness up to the stated symmetries is only for sufficiently large α. The ball threshold is sufficient, not optimal. No claim about complex Fourier zeros or other dimensions follows.

value.rationale: The exact transverse endpoint is the quantitative obstruction in a pre-existing Fourier-zero isoperimetric counterexample, not an arbitrary parameter sample. It supplies the first possible zeros, determines the previously unspecified asymptotic slope, and distinguishes the nearest zero from the boundary point through an explicit curvature correction. The smaller sufficient counterexample threshold is a concrete consequence, not the sole advance.
residual_risks: This does not characterize all finite-α minimizers or settle sharp thresholds in other dimensions.
